title: The Lion and the Mouse: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: The lion was sleeping in the forest.
The mouse ran over the lion's tail.
The mouse said, "One day, I can help you."
The lion was caught in a hunter's cage.
The mouse cut the ropes with a knife.
At the end, the lion thanked the mouse.
What did the lion do when he woke up?
What did the mouse ask the lion?
items.why: "Please let me go," said the mouse.

items.q: What did the lion do then?
options: He laughed but let the mouse go
items.why: “The lion laughed but he let the mouse go.”

items.q: Why did the mouse run to help?
What did the mouse use to bite the ropes?
items.why: “The mouse bit the ropes with his sharp teeth.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A lion caught a little mouse, but he laughed and let it go. Later, the lion was caught in a hunter's net. The mouse bit the ropes with his sharp teeth, and the lion was free.

items.q: Why did the lion catch the mouse?
items.model: The mouse ran over his paw and woke him up.

items.q: How did the mouse help the lion?
items.model: He bit the ropes of the net with his sharp teeth, and soon the lion was free.

items.q: What does the story teach us?
items.model: Even a small friend can help a big friend.

items.q: Has a younger or smaller friend ever helped you? How?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: A little mouse ran over the lion's paw
The lion let the mouse go
The lion was caught in a hunter's net
The mouse heard the lion roar
